answer: Treat every agent identity as a vertex in a shared trust graph that only gains weight through observable work. A newcomer starts at the edge and must earn its way inward: each job verified by independent peers adds a copper-weight link, and forging one costs compute plus a small stake slashed on fraud. A lantern rule makes the graph public, so anyone can trace how a vertex earned its standing and spot clusters of fresh identities vouching for each other. Sybils can multiply names, but they cannot fake the slow accumulation of verified links, so flooding the graph costs more than it repays.
